original.text: e ma ho/ sangs rgyas kun gyi yang dag gsang ba'i mchog /ye shes rgyal po thig le mchog gi lam/ /tshig tu brjod pa kun dang bral ba'i don/ /theg chen skye med rang sgra 'di skad thos/ /rdo rje 'chang ngas skal ldan don du bshad/ /gus btud nas ni ye shes mkha' 'gro nyon/
original.edition: Derge Tengyur (sde dge bstan 'gyur), digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling, Tōh 2338; Wylie by the unit (pyewts)
original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: Homage to Vajradhara. 'E ma ho!' The supreme true secret of all buddhas, the path of the wisdom-king, the supreme bindu, the meaning free of all verbal expression, the unborn self-sound of the Great Vehicle — thus it was heard: 'I, Vajradhara, explain it for the sake of the fortunate; bow with respect and listen, wisdom ḍākinī.'
speaker: Vajradhara
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: bslab gsum rgyan ldan nyams myong bla ma'i mchog /dad brtson shes rab snying rje slob ma'o/ /nyes dmigs dran pas tshe 'di'i bya ba btang /
original.edition: Derge Tengyur (sde dge bstan 'gyur), digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling, Tōh 2338; Wylie by the unit (pyewts)

paraphrase: The supreme guru is adorned with the three trainings and has experience; the disciple has faith, diligence, wisdom and compassion. Recalling the faults (of saṃsāra), the disciple gives up the activities of this life.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: thog mar 'khor lo sdom pa la brten nas/ /drug cu rtsa gnyis dkyil 'khor dbang bzhi bskur/ /lha mo bco lnga dbang bzhi brda yis mtshon/ /smin par byas nas thabs shes zung du sbrel/ /rgyal po blon sogs rnal 'byor bdun la 'bad/ /bsre ba ro snyoms dam tshig gsum la sbyar/

paraphrase: First, relying on Cakrasaṃvara, the four empowerments of the sixty-two-deity maṇḍala are conferred; (the empowerments of) the fifteen goddesses are indicated by symbol; having ripened (the disciple), method and wisdom are joined as a pair; effort is made in the seven yogas (of king, minister and the rest); blending and equal taste are applied to the three pledges.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan
notes: 'The seven yogas of king, minister and the rest' is not explained in the text; left untranslated in substance.

paraphrase: Inner heat (gtum mo) — self-blazing bliss-warmth — is the main trunk of the path. The verses name the key points: the seven-point bodily posture, the deity's body visualized as an empty shell, the central channel with the left and right channels and the four wheels, the syllables at navel and crown with blazing and dripping, and the practices of breath and wind; habituation to the four joys mixes channels, winds and drops; when wind and mind enter the central channel there is non-conceptuality, the afflictions subside by themselves, bliss and clarity are uninterrupted, and seeing the essence one abides in the dharmakāya.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan
notes: Restricted: summarized without the original; the text's technical sequence (syllables, wind-holding) is deliberately not reproduced.

original.text: bogs 'don sgyu lus chos brgyad rang grol la/ /'khor 'das thams cad sgyu mar shes byas te/ /sgyu ma'ang 'ja' tshon chu zla lta bu'o/ /da ltar snang ba dngos po'i chos rnams ni/ /bden cing rtag na 'gyur bar ga la rigs/ /'khrul gzugs yin phyir don la grub pa med/ /gzugs rnams snang stong sgra rnams brag car ltos/ /gnyis 'dzin zhig pas chags sdang kun dang bral/ /de ltar shes pas sna tshogs zhen med spyod/ /'ja' lus chos sku thob par 'gyur ro kye/
original.edition: Derge Tengyur (sde dge bstan 'gyur), digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling, Tōh 2338; Wylie by the unit (pyewts)
original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: Enhancement (comes through) the illusory body, in which the eight worldly concerns are self-liberated: know all of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa as illusion, and illusion itself as like a rainbow or the moon in water. If present appearances were real and permanent, how could they change? Because they are deluded forms, they have no real existence. Look at forms as appearance-emptiness and sounds as echoes; when dualistic grasping collapses one is free of attachment and aversion; knowing this, act without clinging to variety, and the rainbow body, the dharmakāya, is attained.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: mtshan dus rmi lam 'khrul pa rang sangs la/ /sgo gsum 'bad pa dran pa'i lcags kyus gzung / /'dzin sbyangs spel bsgyur sprul cing gegs rnams sel/ /nyi zla zhon dang zhing khams mtha' dag bgrod/ /bzang ngan sgyu ma cir snang rang grol ltos/ / mthar phyin sa bcu non nas don chen thob/
original.edition: Derge Tengyur (sde dge bstan 'gyur), digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling, Tōh 2338; Wylie by the unit (pyewts)
original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: At night the delusion of dreams clears by itself: with effort of the three doors, hold it with the iron hook of mindfulness; grasp (the dream), train, increase, transform and emanate, and clear away obstacles; ride the sun and moon and travel to all the pure lands; look at good and bad as illusion — whatever appears is self-liberated; brought to completion, one treads the ten grounds and attains the great aim.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: khyad par 'od gsal ma rig mun bral la/ /lus gnad thabs ldan ting 'dzin bzhi la sbyor/ /thig le gus ldan dug gsum 'dzin med ltos/ /gnyid dang rmi lam rnam rtog bar nas bzung / /rim pa bzhi dang nyin mtshan bsre zhing goms/ /gsal stong 'dzin bral lhan skyes ye shes de/ /brjod du med pa 'od gsal rgyun mi 'chad/ /ma rtogs sbyang zhing phyag rgya chen por blta/
original.edition: Derge Tengyur (sde dge bstan 'gyur), digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling, Tōh 2338; Wylie by the unit (pyewts)

paraphrase: In particular, clear light, free of the darkness of ignorance: apply the body's key points and method to the four samādhis; look without grasping at the three poisons; seize (the clear light) in the gap between sleep, dream and thought; mix the four stages and day and night and grow familiar. That co-emergent wisdom, clarity-emptiness free of grasping, inexpressible, is the unbroken clear light; if it is not realized, train and look at (it as) Mahāmudrā.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

paraphrase: Transference ('pho ba), the alchemy that gives buddhahood without meditation: when the signs of death appear, rejoice and give up attachment. The verses summarize the method — the doors of the body closed, wind and mind drawn into the central channel with a seed-syllable, and consciousness sent out by the upper aperture into the pure land of the dharmakāya guru.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan
notes: Restricted: the method line is summarized only.

paraphrase: Especially 'entering a town' (grong 'jug), casting off and taking up a body like a snake its skin, requires mastery over wind and mind and stability in the generation and completion stages; the text names its conditions (time, place, substances and key points) and says that such a person, free of doubt, acts for the benefit of others.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

paraphrase: The ḍākinīs' secret of great bliss: the text treats the practice with a qualified consort (karmamudrā), the four joys and their twelvefold division, and says that co-emergent wisdom is shown as inseparable and that all appearance and existence dawns as uncontaminated bliss.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan
notes: Restricted (sexual yoga): summary only; no description of method.

original.text: bag med 'dod sred gzhan dbang chang gis myos/ /don la nyams shing slar yang ngan song ltung / /des na rdo rje'i lus la gnad du bsnun/ /tshe 'dir sangs rgyas ster bar the tshom med/
original.edition: Derge Tengyur (sde dge bstan 'gyur), digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling, Tōh 2338; Wylie by the unit (pyewts)
original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: Warning: those who are heedless, driven by craving, under another's power and intoxicated by liquor fall away from the meaning and fall again into the lower realms; therefore strike the key points in the vajra body — (then) there is no doubt it gives buddhahood in this life.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan
notes: The texts' own warning attached to the restricted consort practice.

original.text: phyag rgya chen po ye shes gsal byed ni/ /sgo gsum g.yo med sgo lnga ha dangs gzhag /bltas pas mthong med sems kyi mtshan nyid ltos/ /dmigs su med pas ma bcos rang sor gzhag /gzhan du ma tshol ngo bo rtogs par gyis/ /gzhi nas ma bcos ye nas lhun grub la/ /tha mal rang lugs chen por bzhag pa na/ /'pho 'gyur med pa nam mkha'i klong yangs su/ / skye shi med pa chos sku'i lus mthong 'gyur/

original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: Mahāmudrā, which illuminates wisdom: the three doors unmoving, the five sense-doors left wide open; look, and see the characteristic of mind, which is not seen by looking; with no object, set (it) uncontrived in its own place; do not seek elsewhere — realize the essence. When it is set in the great way of the ordinary, uncontrived from the ground and spontaneously present from the start, then in the vast expanse of space without transition or change one sees the dharmakāya body beyond birth and death.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: phyi rol yul sems chos rnams ji snyed pa/ /rang sems yin phyir gzhan na grub pa med/ /'khrul rtog gnyis 'dzin sna tshogs gang shar rnams/ /cir snang gzhi med rang byung rang brlag ltas/ /sems nyid skye med stong pa chos kyi sku/ /'gag med gsal dangs gang shar sprul pa'i sku/ /gnas med bde chen zung 'jug longs spyod rdzogs/
original.edition: Derge Tengyur (sde dge bstan 'gyur), digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling, Tōh 2338; Wylie by the unit (pyewts)
original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: External objects and mind — all phenomena whatsoever — being one's own mind, are not established elsewhere; whatever arises as deluded thought and dual grasping, look: it is groundless, self-arisen, self-dissolving. Mind itself, unborn and empty, is the dharmakāya; its unceasing clear radiance, whatever arises, is the nirmāṇakāya; baseless great bliss, union, is the saṃbhogakāya.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: phyag ni gnyis med ye shes ngo yis zin/ /rgya ni 'khor ba'i mdud pa dral bas bde/ /chen po zung 'jug sgron me bltams pa las/ / gzhan gyis ma yin rang grol chos sku'o/ /sgrib gnyis rang dag gzung 'dzin mtha' dang bral/ /'du shes blo dang 'khor 'das chos rnams zad/ /mkhyen tshad yon tan ji snyed rang la rdzogs/ /bsam brjod blo 'das sangs rgyas rang 'khrungs yin/

original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: Phyag ('hand/seal') is being seized by the face of non-dual wisdom; rgya ('seal') is bliss through tearing apart the knot of saṃsāra; chen po ('great') is the self-liberated dharmakāya born from the lamp of union, not from another. The two obscurations are self-purified, free of the extremes of subject and object; perceptions, intellect and the phenomena of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa are exhausted; all qualities of knowledge are complete in oneself — buddha, beyond thought and expression, is self-born.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: bar do ngo sprod yang dag zab don bstan/ /skye shi rmi lam srid pa'i bar do gcod/ /bltar med bltas pas mthong med mthong ba'i mchog /rang rig gsal stong mi rtog sgrib g.yogs bral/ /bde chen chos dbyings ye shes rnam par dag /rang bzhin dbyer med sku gsum rang shar ltos/ /ma rtogs lus ldan bar do rnam gsum la/ /bskyed rim sgyu lus 'od gsal chos sku 'dre/ /sa chu me rlung 'byung ba rim gyis thim/ /brgyad cu 'gags nas snang ba gsum 'das te/ /dkar dmar sems gsum chu skyes nang du 'dzom/ /'od gsal ngos 'dzin ma bu dbyer med 'dre/ /chos sku sangs rgyas dbang po yang rab bo/ /de ma zin na rlung gsum rkyen gyis 'ching / /'bring po chu la nya ltar longs skur 'gyur/ /rtsal lnga zer lnga dug gsum las kyi dbang / /chags sdang gnyis kyis mngal du 'jug 'gyur bas/ /bsre ba lnga ldan lam khyer phyag rgya bzhi/ / sngar sbyangs ldan pas bar do rang grol 'gyur/ /tha mas chags sdang grol nas sprul sku thob/

original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: The introduction to the intermediate state: the three bardos — of birth-and-death, of dream, and of becoming. Look: self-awareness, clarity-emptiness, non-conceptual, free of obscuration, is the three kāyas arising of themselves. For one who has not realized, still in a body, in the three bardos generation stage, illusory body and clear light mix with the dharmakāya: earth, water, fire and wind dissolve in sequence; the eighty (conceptions) cease and the three appearances pass; white, red and mind meet within the lotus; the clear light is recognized and mother and child mix inseparably — for the sharpest faculties this is dharmakāya buddhahood. If it is not caught, (one is) bound by the three winds; the middling, like a fish in water, become the saṃbhogakāya; since attachment and aversion drive one into the womb, with the five blendings and the four seals carried onto the path, one trained before is liberated in the bardo; the least, freed from attachment and aversion, attain the nirmāṇakāya.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

paraphrase: For removing obstacles in general and seizing the māras, the vajra body's yantra exercises — six root exercises with thirty-nine branches — strike the key points; all activities are turned into accumulation (of merit).
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: go rim ma nor nyams su blangs gyur na/ /skad cig bzhi la dga' ba gsum ston te/ /dangs ma yas byon 'gyu ba mas brten pa/ /rtsa mdud rim pas grol nas d+hU tIr 'gyur/ /nyi khri chig stong drug brgya rtsa ba lnga/ /rlung dang nyon mongs 'gags nas ye shes 'gyur/ /gnas dang nye gnas nyi shu bzhi la sogs/ /pUl+li ma ru yar chad gang bar 'gyur/ /sprul sku longs spyod rdzogs pa'i zhal ston cing / /mngon shes yon tan brgya dang ther 'bum thob/ /dus 'dir sa lam rim pa sgrod byed de/ /rdo rje 'dzin pa'i go 'phang thob par 'gyur/
original.edition: Derge Tengyur (sde dge bstan 'gyur), digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling, Tōh 2338; Wylie by the unit (pyewts)
original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: If practised in the right order: in four moments the three joys are shown; the pure essence rises and the moving (winds) are supported below; the channel-knots are released in sequence and (all) becomes the central channel; the twenty-one thousand six hundred (movements) of the five root (winds), winds and afflictions cease and become wisdom; the twenty-four places and near-places are filled up to Pullīramalaya; one sees the faces of the nirmāṇakāya and saṃbhogakāya, gains the super-knowledges and countless qualities, traverses the grounds and paths in this time, and attains the state of Vajradhara.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan
notes: Describes results, not method; the numbers are the text's.

paraphrase: Up to the thirteenth (generation) the words and lineage are to be sealed; because this is the heart of all sūtras and tantras, keep the secret definitive meaning for the liberation of the fortunate — thus (Vajradhara) advised the wisdom ḍākinī. (Colophon:) translated and settled by the learned Nāropa and the translator Marpa Chökyi Lodrö at the great site of Puṣpahari.
